title: 1961 AHSME Problem 14
statement: A rhombus is given with one diagonal twice the length of the other diagonal. Express the side of the rhombus in terms of \(K,\) where \(K\) is the area of the rhombus in square inches.

solutions.text:
Let the diagonals be \(d\) and \(2d.\) Then \(K=\frac{d(2d)}{2}=d^2.\) A side has length \[ \begin{aligned} \sqrt{\left(\frac d2\right)^2+d^2} &=\frac{\sqrt5}{2}d\\ &=\frac12\sqrt{5K}. \end{aligned} \] This is not among the first four choices.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the diagonals be \(d\) and \(2d\), then use the rhombus area formula
Half-diagonals form the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is a side
